title: Perceptions of High School Graduates and Educators Regarding a Mathematics Intervention for College and Career Readiness
extended_summary:
This dissertation examines a local mathematics achievement problem at Midwest High School in Iowa, where more than 68% of 11th-grade students from 2017 through 2024 did not meet the ACT college- and career-readiness benchmark in mathematics despite the school’s use of the Kendall Hunt Illustrative Mathematics (KHIM) curriculum. The study asks why the curriculum did not appear to improve outcomes and what changes graduates and educators believed would better support student success.

The study used a basic qualitative design with semistructured interviews. Participants included eight high school graduates and four non-administrative educators from Midwest High School. The author analyzed interview transcripts using in vivo coding to identify themes in participants’ perceptions of learning and teaching with KHIM. Participants generally viewed the curriculum as supporting procedural skill, fluency, peer collaboration, and conceptual integrity, but they also reported insufficient support, guidance, practice, timely feedback, and instructional presence.

The project component proposes integrating lower-cost generative AI tools into mathematics instruction to provide personalized practice, real-world applications, timely feedback, and more instructional presence. The dissertation positions this as a means to improve college- and career-readiness at Midwest High School. It is not an empirical study of Khanmigo or any AI system, and it does not report achievement effects from an intervention trial.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a qualitative dissertation focused on perceptions and a proposed AI-enabled project, not a rigorous intervention study. It provides contextual evidence and implementation rationale, but no causal evaluation of Khanmigo or any AI tool on student outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No empirical effect on science learning outcomes is reported, and the paper is not about Khanmigo or science instruction. The text only suggests potential future benefits of generative AI in mathematics, without measurable impact data.

interventions.use_case: The dissertation proposes integrating lower-cost generative AI tools into mathematics instruction to provide personalized practice, real-world application opportunities, timely feedback, and increased instructional presence.
